checked.what_was_checked: Seat-versus-mechanism attribution, the shipped workhorse binding, topology, parent/child rate attribution, cache-order effects, and whether modelled Codex dollars represent the operational cost being decided.
Host units, participant-specific rates, token-kind composition, cliff pricing, item denominators, percent-saving orientation, output-dominance population, and paired comparison basis.

Controls 0–9 against missing or extra participants, wrong rates, zero-valued parser fields, zero and partial attempts, checker vacuity, inheritance, cache carryover, and false infrastructure classification.
Stage-1 and Stage-2 decision rules, zero-pass outcomes, confidence-bound construction, multiplicity across confirmatory cells, output-dominance eligibility, and the quality margin.
Claims against the prior measurements, spawn-target definitions, parser excerpt, cross-host record, and round-1 dispositions, including whether revision-2 repairs close the cited findings.
Internal consistency and cell-level application of the supplied rate ratios, cache lifetimes, token fields, long-context multipliers, fork asymmetry, and OAuth billing facts.

findings.anchor_quote: | delegated-cheap-lowE | P | isolated spawn | luna / low (haiku / low) | 1 | same |
findings.input_or_condition: A Claude delegated-cheap-lowE cell clears the KEEP thresholds.
findings.signal_emitted: The experiment emits KEEP for the shipped `workhorse` target on evidence from `claude-haiku-4-5 / low`.
findings.truth_instead: The bundled shipped Claude workhorse is `claude-opus-5 / medium`; neither cheap arm nor the sonnet/high arm runs that binding. The result establishes nothing about the target whose retention is being decided.
findings.evidence: BUNDLE 3 gives `model: claude-opus-5` and `effort: medium` for `claude/agents/workhorse.md`. The target fixes P at opus/xhigh and tests haiku/low, haiku/high, and sonnet/high, leaving opus/medium absent.
findings.change_required: Add a decision arm pinned to each host's exact shipped workhorse model and effort, and make KEEP/DELETE for `workhorse` quantify over that arm; candidate-model arms must have separate, explicitly scoped verdicts.

findings.anchor_quote: **Topology is fixed**: one child per run, doing all M items, sequential, one pristine
findings.input_or_condition: A generated repetition contains at least two independent edits, as permitted by the M-item task, and the sequential one-child cell reaches a terminal threshold.
findings.signal_emitted: The design emits a workhorse KEEP or DELETE verdict while claiming to exercise its contract as written.
findings.truth_instead: The deployed workhorse contract says two or more independent items spawn in parallel. The measured sequential batch has different child count, cache injection, and interference, so it is not the deployed routing behavior.
findings.evidence: BUNDLE 3 says in the workhorse description: `two or more independent items spawn in parallel.` Revision 2 instead fixes one child to perform all M items sequentially and still says the task exercises the contract as written.
findings.change_required: Either make every M-item fixture explicitly non-independent and scope the verdict to that case, or run the contract-required fan-out with all spawned participants included in the ledger and estimator before issuing the ship verdict.
findings.caused_by_change: Revision 2's topology repair fixed every run to one sequential child while retaining a gate about the deployed workhorse contract.

findings.anchor_quote: - **Codex** — an OAuth subscription pays no per-run dollar. Tokens by kind are measured;
findings.input_or_condition: A Codex cell has at least 25% saving under the nominal rate table while both arms have the same zero marginal OAuth dollar charge and their rate-limit debits are unknown.
findings.signal_emitted: The modelled-dollar statistic can trigger KEEP as evidence that the shipped cheap seat costs less operationally.
findings.truth_instead: Only a hypothetical rate-weighted token figure is lower. No per-run cash saving occurred, and the scarce subscription quantity identified by the bundled record—rate-limit budget—was not measured.
findings.evidence: BUNDLE 2 states that Codex cost cannot be measured in money under OAuth and that the comparable scarce quantity is tokens and rate-limit budget. The target acknowledges no per-run dollar but nevertheless feeds modelled dollars into the same KEEP/DELETE predicates.
findings.change_required: Remove Codex modelled dollars from the operational ship gate unless a measured mapping to subscription rate-limit debits is added; otherwise give Codex a separate verdict explicitly limited to hypothetical API-rate-equivalent cost.

findings.anchor_quote: differential probe instead: per-turn versus cumulative summation of the same rollout
findings.input_or_condition: For a Codex delegated-cheap run, an implementation sums the sol parent and luna child token kinds and applies luna rates to the aggregate, or otherwise maps a participant to the wrong rate vector.
findings.signal_emitted: The Codex known-opposite control passes because per-turn and cumulative token sums agree, while the understated modelled run cost can clear KEEP.
findings.truth_instead: The cost is the sum of each participant's token kinds multiplied by that participant's receipted model rates; agreement between two aggregations of the same usage does not validate that mapping.
findings.evidence: The treatment row contains a sol parent and luna child whose supplied rates differ by up to 20×. Codex has no measured bill, and the revised differential probe tests aggregation only; the field goldens test token values, not model-to-rate assignment.
findings.change_required: Specify the participant-indexed formula `sum(participant, kind, usage × participant_rate)` and add independently hand-calculated mixed-model goldens that fail wrong-seat rates, aggregation-before-pricing, and swapped participant mappings.

findings.anchor_quote: subagent TTL. A later arm must not be cheaper because an earlier arm warmed its prefix.
findings.input_or_condition: Claude uses the design's one-hour cache-write bucket and two same-model arms execute 6–59 minutes apart; the R=5 counterbalance leaves one decision arm with more warm-cache exposure than its comparator.
findings.signal_emitted: The later arm reports a lower measured cost and the difference is attributed to its seat, potentially crossing KEEP.
findings.truth_instead: The difference is caused by the preceding arm's still-live prefix. Waiting past only the five-minute TTL does not make a one-hour entry cold, and five repetitions cannot exactly balance all positions or pairwise carryover among six Claude arms.
findings.evidence: The same Common basis section explicitly maps `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` and prices one-hour cache writes, while the cache-order repair waits only beyond the five-minute subagent TTL. Round 1 already identified cross-arm prefix warming.
findings.change_required: Isolate Claude cache identity or separate same-model arm executions beyond the maximum one-hour lifetime and verify the intended cold/warm state from the token receipt; do not allow counterbalancing alone to satisfy this control.

findings.anchor_quote: **Long-context cliff (Codex).** Every run records its peak input. A run above 272K is
findings.input_or_condition: A multi-turn Codex participant has both below-272K turns and one above-272K turn, while only peak input and run-aggregate token kinds are retained.
findings.signal_emitted: The whole run is priced at the published multipliers, inflating that arm's modelled cost and potentially manufacturing a cheap-seat saving.
findings.truth_instead: Threshold exposure must be applied to the token kinds belonging to the threshold-crossing billed turn or request. Peak plus aggregate totals cannot distinguish those tokens from below-cliff tokens.
findings.evidence: The rate table makes pricing conditional on being above 272K, and Control 1 acknowledges per-turn usage. The cliff rule nevertheless promotes the run as a whole from one peak without requiring per-turn token-kind allocation.
findings.change_required: Retain the context size and five token-kind counts for every billed turn and apply the cliff multipliers turn by turn before summing the run.
findings.caused_by_change: Revision 2 replaced above-cliff exclusion with a run-level peak flag and multiplier pricing without retaining per-turn threshold exposure.

findings.anchor_quote: payload showing every one of the five fields, with cache write and thinking **nonzero**
findings.input_or_condition: The Stage-0 fresh-child golden legitimately has zero cache-read tokens, while the parser's cache-read extraction is hard-coded to zero or reads the wrong path; a later decision run has nonzero cache reads.
findings.signal_emitted: The field-existence control passes, then the modelled run cost omits cached-input charges and can report a false saving.
findings.truth_instead: A zero-valued captured field proves neither extraction nor field identity. The later cached tokens have a nonzero supplied rate and must appear in cost.
findings.evidence: Control 5 forces only cache write and thinking to be nonzero. BUNDLE 2 contains measured nonzero Codex cache reuse, and the target assigns cache read a nonzero price. The conservation identity can still pass if uncached input is derived after the broken cached value.
findings.change_required: Use parser goldens with distinct nonzero sentinel values for every physical token field, including cache read and both Claude cache-write lifetime buckets, and require each omission or swap mutation to fail.

findings.anchor_quote: attempted items, zero output tokens, a missing participant — is excluded and reported.
findings.input_or_condition: A correctly dispatched cheap child runs and returns a refusal or makes no edit, so zero of the M assigned items are attempted even though participant and host receipts exist.
findings.signal_emitted: The harness labels the run an infrastructure failure and excludes it; subsequent counted runs can therefore show non-inferior quality or KEEP.
findings.truth_instead: This is a genuine 0-for-M subject outcome. Intention-to-treat requires its full cost and zero passes to remain in the cheap arm.
findings.evidence: The task always assigns M items. The estimator retains full cost for zero passing items when attempts are nonzero, but Control 6 still uses zero attempts alone as an exclusion condition. BUNDLE 5 identifies the same round-1 failure mode.
findings.change_required: Define the intention-to-treat attempted denominator as the M identities assigned after a receipted dispatch. Distinguish a runner that never invoked the subject through dispatch and participant receipts, and count a valid refusal or no-op as 0/M.

findings.anchor_quote: 3. **Denominator.** The generated manifest's item identity set, the run's attempted set,
findings.input_or_condition: A valid M=40 child attempts 39 named edits and omits one, while the verifier can issue pass/fail receipts for all 40 assigned identities.
findings.signal_emitted: The three-set equality control emits a denominator/control failure instead of retaining the run, so an ordinary subject omission is removed from the quality sample.
findings.truth_instead: The omitted assigned identity is a failed item, not missing infrastructure; the truthful outcome is its full run cost with at most 39/40 passing.
findings.evidence: Control 3 requires actual attempted identities to equal the manifest, while Control 6 says a nonzero-attempt run with any pass count is a counted outcome. Those rules disagree for every proper nonempty subset.
findings.change_required: Use the assigned manifest as the fixed intention-to-treat set, require the verifier to receipt every assigned identity, and record the child's touched or claimed set separately; assigned-but-unattempted identities must score as failures.
findings.caused_by_change: Revision 2 introduced the three-set equality control while also retaining nonzero partial attempts as counted subject outcomes.

findings.anchor_quote: below **40%** of modelled cost is relabelled *not output-dominated* and reported
findings.input_or_condition: A cell's median cost shares are 35% visible output, 30% thinking, and 35% input/cache.
findings.signal_emitted: The design labels the cell `not output-dominated`.
findings.truth_instead: Under the design's own rate mapping, 65% of the bill lands in output-priced kinds because thinking is billed as output; the emitted label says the opposite of the stated bill-location construct.
findings.evidence: The five-kind table says thinking is billed as output for both vendors, and the P paragraph says thinking can be 57% of output. The classifier includes only visible output in its numerator.
findings.change_required: Classify bill location using visible output plus thinking, or replace the claim and label with the narrower `visible-output share ≥40%` everywhere it is used.
findings.caused_by_change: Revision 2 introduced the visible-output 40% relabeling to answer round 1's unmeasured write-dominance finding.

findings.anchor_quote: - **DELETE** only if, for **every** pre-named cell at R=5, the **upper** 90% bound of the
findings.input_or_condition: Every Stage-2 cell is relabelled `not output-dominated`, and every saving upper bound is at most 20%.
findings.signal_emitted: The universal predicate emits DELETE for the write-dominated-work question.
findings.truth_instead: The experiment observed no cell in the population named by the question, so it has no evidence for deleting a seat on write-dominated work; the valid result is inconclusive.
findings.evidence: The Task section says non-output-dominated cells are reported separately and never pooled, but neither KEEP nor DELETE conditions eligibility on the output-dominance label; both quantify over every pre-named cell.
findings.change_required: Define contrast eligibility before applying thresholds, require both compared arms to satisfy the in-scope construct under a fixed rule, and force INCONCLUSIVE when no eligible write-dominated contrast exists.
findings.caused_by_change: Revision 2 introduced output-dominance relabeling without adding it as an eligibility condition to KEEP or DELETE.

findings.anchor_quote: - **KEEP** if, in any pre-named cell at R=5, the **lower** 90% bound of the saving on the
findings.input_or_condition: Delegated-same costs $100 per verified item and delegated-cheap costs $80 with negligible uncertainty.
findings.signal_emitted: An implementation using `(same / cheap) − 1` reports 25% and emits KEEP.
findings.truth_instead: The baseline-relative cost reduction `(same − cheap) / same` is 20%, while the separately declared raw contrast `cheap − same` is negative. The design has not registered a sign or denominator, so no 25% decision is established.
findings.evidence: Revision 2 registers the ratio-of-sums cell statistic and names contrasts as `delegated-cheap − delegated-same`, but never defines the transformation called `saving`. The two common normalizations give opposite threshold outcomes on the stated input.
findings.change_required: Define saving algebraically, including its baseline denominator and sign—for example `1 − Ccheap/Csame`—and construct every point estimate and bound on that registered estimand.

findings.anchor_quote: repetition-level analysis and one-sided bounds. Mid and fork arms carry no evidence about
findings.input_or_condition: At R=5, one cheap repetition has positive cost and zero passing items, the other four pass items, and the cell's ratio-of-sums remains finite; dropping the undefined per-run ratio gives a lower 90% saving bound above 25%, while a paired ratio-of-sums resampling over all five blocks gives a bound below 25%.
findings.signal_emitted: A conforming implementation can omit the zero-pass pair from its unspecified bound calculation and emit KEEP.
findings.truth_instead: Control 6 requires the zero-pass run and its cost to remain. The full five-pair evidence does not establish the registered threshold under the bound that retains it.
findings.evidence: The point estimator is specified as a ratio of sums, but `paired repetition-level analysis and one-sided bounds` does not select a t, bootstrap, permutation, Fieller, or other interval construction, nor define zero-denominator behavior. Zero-pass repetitions are explicitly allowed.
findings.change_required: Pre-register one executable bound algorithm on paired `(cost, passed, assigned)` block sufficient statistics, including zero-pass and zero-total-denominator rules, and use the same fixed algorithm for saving and pass-rate bounds.
findings.caused_by_change: Revision 2 introduced one-sided bounds and retained zero-pass outcomes without defining a bound estimator that can consume those outcomes.

findings.anchor_quote: - **KEEP** if, in any pre-named cell at R=5, the **lower** 90% bound of the saving on the
findings.input_or_condition: All 36 decision contrasts—2 cheap arms × 3 sizes × 3 difficulty levels × 2 hosts—have true saving below 25%, quality is safely non-inferior, and sampling noise puts at least one pointwise lower 90% bound above 25%.
findings.signal_emitted: The any-cell predicate emits KEEP and presents existence of a qualifying cell as established.
findings.truth_instead: The selected crossing is a family-search false positive; pointwise 90% bounds do not provide 90% coverage for the assertion that at least one of 36 cells exceeds the threshold.
findings.evidence: The predicate remains `in any pre-named cell` with only pointwise 90% bounds. BUNDLE 5 explicitly reported the same round-1 multiplicity defect; revision 2 added R=5 and bounds but no simultaneous correction or confirmation step.
findings.change_required: Use a pre-registered simultaneous lower-bound procedure for the full KEEP family or require an independently replicated confirmatory cell selected without reusing the search data.

findings.anchor_quote: estimator is ≥25% *and* the pass rate is non-inferior (lower bound of the difference
findings.input_or_condition: At M=160, delegated-same passes 160/160 in every repetition and cheap passes 154/160 in every repetition; its saving lower bound exceeds 25% and its quality-difference lower bound is at least −5 points.
findings.signal_emitted: The rule emits KEEP as the answer to a question requiring equal or better verified quality.
findings.truth_instead: Cheap is consistently 3.75 percentage points, or six verified items per run, worse. A −5-point non-inferiority margin is not equal-or-better quality.
findings.evidence: The Question requires `equal or better verified quality`, while KEEP explicitly permits a lower bound as low as −5 points.
findings.change_required: Set the quality criterion to a lower bound of at least zero, or change the experiment's question and terminal verdict to explicitly authorize and name a loss of up to five percentage points.

boundary_notes: External official documentation, live prices, model availability, effort support, cache-key semantics, and raw vendor schemas were not fetched; R6 was limited to consistency and application within the packet.

BUNDLE 4 contains only `_parse_claude`. Claims about `_parse_codex`, `seat_problem()`, `run.py`, `naive_edit`, Claude child-transcript accounting, and `parent_thread_id` lookup could not be verified from bundled source.
The Codex workhorse definition is not bundled. The shipped-binding finding is therefore scoped to Claude, whose exact workhorse definition is present.

The full revision-1 design and raw benchmark runs are absent. Provenance classifications use Revision 2's stated changes and BUNDLE 5's round-1 finding summaries; an exact textual diff could not be verified.
